name: bounded-self-nesting
body:
A section declaration may accept its own template, directly or through a cycle, when a declaration on the cycle carries `max_depth: N` — a positive integer. A declaration's `max_depth` belongs to the declaration that carries it and bounds how many times that declaration's section recurs in one containment chain: an instance the declaration produces has at most N enclosing instances that resolve to the same template it does, so its `.item.depth` is at most N. Direct self-acceptance — one declaration that accepts its own template — is the one-template case of this rule, where the accepted template is the declaring template and the bound is that template's `.item.depth`. The loader walks the declaration graph bounded by these declarations, so a self-referencing or cyclic declared-section acceptance is valid: content may nest the repeated template up to the bound, and the walk stops at the bound instead of reporting a cycle. When several declarations on one cycle carry `max_depth`, each enforces its own bound independently, and the loader's walk stops at the first bound the chain reaches. The loader walks each bounded cycle to the longest chain its bounds allow — the cycle's composition prefix plus the levels the bounds admit — and that heading-level chain is measured against the six-heading-level bound (requirements.constraint.section-depth-limit): a cycle whose longest bounded walk would exceed six heading levels is refused at load as a templates error, the depth-limit error naming the chain and the `max_depth` that produces it, so every declared `max_depth` is reachable in content. A reference cycle whose declarations carry no `max_depth` is a templates error, the chain error of requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain; bounded self-nesting is the one accepted declared-section cycle. `max_depth` is a positive integer on a section declaration; a value that is not a positive integer is a templates error naming the offending `template.yaml`.

The authored Markdown syntax is unchanged: a self-nested instance is a heading one level deeper than its parent, naming the declaring section slot (slide-sections), so nesting depth is heading depth and no new author-facing syntax exists. Depth is enforced when the content is parsed, at every level: an instance the bounded declaration produces whose `.item.depth` would exceed the declaration's `max_depth` is a slide error path-qualified to the offending slide file with its containment chain (error-reporting, nested-section-validation). The error names the declaration that carries the bound, with the message `section "<declared name>": nesting deeper than max_depth N` — `<declared name>` is the bounded declaration's section slot name (`loop` for a direct self-accepting `loop` declaration, `b` for a bounded declaration named `b`) and N is that declaration's `max_depth`.

Each nested instance carries the ordinary reserved section context (template-context, item-context). `.item.depth` is the instance's self-nesting depth: the number of enclosing instances whose resolved template is the same template — 0 at the outermost instance of that template in the containment chain and +1 at each self-nested level. `.item.parent` is the enclosing instance at every level; `.item.section` is the declared section name at that level (for example `events` at the top and `loop` nested); `.item.index` and `.item.count` are the instance's real position within its group of siblings at each level. A declaration's `max_depth` bounds the instances of the template it accepts, so `.item.depth` is the quantity a declaration bounds: an instance the declaration produces at `.item.depth` N is accepted and one whose `.item.depth` would exceed N is the depth error above. For direct self-acceptance the accepted template is the declaring template, so the bound is that template's `.item.depth`; for a multi-template cycle a declaration bounds the `.item.depth` of the template it accepts (the template of the instances its section produces), which is a different quantity from the `.item.depth` of the declaring template — the two coincide for direct self-acceptance and differ when a template is produced by more than one declaration.

A `section` helper call is a composition reference but not a section declaration, so it carries no max_depth and a helper-closed cycle is a templates error (section-helper-load-checks); bounded self-nesting widens the declared-section acceptance graph only and leaves section-helper pass-through rendering unchanged.

AC: a template that declares a `loop` section accepting itself with `max_depth: 1` loads with no cycle error, and a slide nesting `# events` › `## loop` parses and renders, the nested `loop` instance reading `.item.depth` 1, its `.item.parent` the enclosing `events` instance, its `.item.section` `loop`, and its `.item.index`/`.item.count` its real position among its `loop` siblings; a `### loop` nested under a `## loop` (self-nesting depth 2) is a slide error carrying the message `section "loop": nesting deeper than max_depth 1`; a two-template cycle — template `a` declaring a `b` section that accepts template `b` with `max_depth: 1`, and template `b` declaring an `a` section that accepts template `a` with no `max_depth` — loads with no cycle error, and a slide nesting `# a` › `## b` › `### a` › `#### b` is accepted, the second `b` instance (one enclosing `b` instance, `.item.depth` 1) satisfying its declaration's `max_depth: 1`, while a `##### a` › `###### b` continuation makes a third `b` instance with two enclosing `b` instances and is a slide error naming the bounded declaration with the message `section "b": nesting deeper than max_depth 1`; the same self-accepting declaration without `max_depth` is refused at load with the chain error `section template reference cycle: sections/loop → sections/loop`; a `max_depth` that is not a positive integer is a templates error naming the `template.yaml`; a slide → `events` → `loop` chain whose `loop` declaration carries `max_depth: 5` — five `loop` headings under the `events` and slide headings, seven heading levels in all — is refused at load with the depth-limit templates error naming the chain and `max_depth: 5`, because every declared `max_depth` is walked to its full depth; one template that declares `loop` accepting itself with `max_depth: 1` replaces the near-identical timeline-event and loop-event templates, rendering a top `events` instance holding `loop` children that hold no further `loop` children; the authored Markdown syntax is unchanged; a `section`-helper cycle is refused at load.
